# Regula

> Open-source CLI tool for EU AI Act compliance. Combines code scanning with governance questionnaires: scans codebases for risk indicators, classifies AI systems into the Act's four risk tiers (prohibited, high-risk, limited-risk, minimal-risk), and provides structured self-assessments for organisational obligations code cannot verify. Runs locally with zero external dependencies -- no API calls, no data leaves the machine. Install: `pipx install regula-ai`.
> **Not affiliated with Regula Forensics** (regula.com, identity verification). This is Regula the EU AI Act compliance CLI at getregula.com.

Regula combines two approaches: (1) static code analysis for risk patterns, dependency security, credential exposure, and bias indicators, and (2) questionnaire-based assessment for organisational obligations like risk management systems (Article 9), quality management (Article 17), fundamental rights impact assessments (Article 27), and post-market monitoring (Article 72). It explicitly documents what it cannot do -- see docs/what-regula-does-not-do.md.

## FAQ

- **What is Regula?** An open-source CLI that scans Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, Go, Rust, C, and C++ code for EU AI Act risk patterns. It classifies systems into the Act's four risk tiers, maps findings to Articles 5-15, generates compliance gap assessments, and produces auditor-ready evidence packs. Runs fully offline with zero dependencies.
- **What does Regula NOT do?** It does not determine final legal risk classification (that depends on intended purpose and deployment context, which are business decisions). It does not verify organisational compliance processes (Articles 9, 17, 27, 72). It does not replace legal advice. See [what-regula-does-not-do.md](https://github.com/kuzivaai/getregula/blob/main/docs/what-regula-does-not-do.md) for the full scope statement.
- **What frameworks does Regula map to?** EU AI Act, GDPR, DORA, NIS2, ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF, OWASP LLM Top 10, OWASP Agentic Top 10, UK AI principles, Colorado SB 25-189, and others (12 frameworks total via `references/framework_crosswalk.yaml`).
- **When are the EU AI Act deadlines?** Article 5 prohibitions: 2 Feb 2025 (already enforceable). GPAI obligations: 2 Aug 2025 (already enforceable). High-risk (Annex III): deferred to 2 Dec 2027 under the Digital Omnibus provisional agreement of 7 May 2026, approved by European Parliament on 16 June 2026 (pending Council adoption and OJ publication). Annex I product-embedded: deferred to 2 Aug 2028. Code of Practice on AI content marking: finalised 10 Jun 2026.
- **Does the EU AI Act apply outside the EU?** Yes. Article 2(1)(c) applies extraterritorially to any provider or deployer whose AI system output is used within the EU, regardless of where the company is established.
- **How accurate is Regula?** Published precision on a random corpus of 115 real-world findings: 83.5%. See [benchmarks](https://github.com/kuzivaai/getregula/blob/main/docs/benchmarks/PRECISION_RECALL_2026_04.md) for methodology and confidence intervals.
